lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to use traversal to calculate an average and find the maximum and minimum values in a list.
Traverse to get the total, then divide by length of list.
Traverse: if item i > max, set max to item i.
At the end, max holds the biggest value.
Start min as item 1, not 0 — otherwise 0 might win wrongly.
Averages and extremes turn raw numbers into facts you can act on: “Saturday was the hottest day.”
Python has built-in sum, max and min — but inside they work exactly like the loops you are writing.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
